“Inﬂation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon.” So wrote Milton
Friedman, the great economist who won the Nobel Prize in economics in 1976.
The quantity theory of money leads us to agree that the growth in the quantity
of money is the primary determinant of the inﬂation rate. Y et Friedman’s claim
is empirical, not theoretical. T o evaluate his claim, and to judge the usefulness
of our theory, we need to look at data on money and prices.
